cells.title: Design review
cells.task:
You review the plan in a session of your own: you did not write it, so look for what its writer cannot see. Read the
principles, and whole each file of decisions whose topic the plan touches. The plan is `plan_owner`, `plan_agent`,
`acceptance`, `questions` and `tree_edits`.

Judge it only by what it was made for (what `background` asks) and the repository's rules, on each of these points:
1. Whether it does what `background` asks, no less and no more, and settles what `found` left to the deep research.
2. Its design by the engineering rules: the responsibilities, interfaces and representations it touches, one place
   for each thing, nothing that no current work needs.
3. The acceptance: whether each condition can be decided, a wrong result would fail it, and together they cover what
   `background` asks.
4. The questions: a question a fact could settle or that is cheap to change later; a choice only the owner can make
   that no question asks; a question not marked in `plan_owner`.
5. A decision of the tree the plan goes against, or a rule later works must follow, that no entry of `tree_edits`
   covers.

`plan_review`, every point at once, and none with `plan_ok` yes. Leave out what you are not sure is better.

main's tree in wording and place, not in meaning. Start from a test that shows what the change is for, red on the code

blocks.what: Whether every question of the work that stands has the owner's answer: `answered` once each has, or none stands; `waiting` while one has not.

writes.text: Every question of the work has the owner's answer.

blocks.name: background
blocks.what: Why the item exists: what was found, what must be done and where it is needed. Written before the work, by whoever made the item.

blocks.name: better_found
blocks.what: yes when thinking the plan through again found a better way, and the plan was written again for it; no otherwise.

blocks.name: check
blocks.what: What the check before the merge says to the cell it judges.

blocks.name: checked
blocks.what: yes when the work's branch passed the check before the merge, against main as it was then; no otherwise.

blocks.name: code
blocks.what: What changed, by module and behaviour, and the commit on the work's branch that holds it all.

blocks.name: decisions
blocks.what: Each decision the code makes that the plan does not record, with why, in `owner.language`: read by the owner on the page and judged by the review.

blocks.name: deep_needed
blocks.what: Whether the plan needs the deep research first: yes only when the direction rests on a fact that cannot be checked in a round or two, or on trying several ways first. Nothing else is a reason: a choice for the owner is a question, a fact the history holds is looked up, and an item that contradicts itself is settled by the facts.

blocks.name: evidence
blocks.what: For each acceptance condition, what shows it on that commit (tests with results after and before the change, a measurement, a CI job, or where to read in the diff); each test added, extended or weakened, with what it catches or why; each new test with how long it runs alone and why that time is worth it; a test that cannot run on the code before the change, with why.

blocks.name: found
blocks.what: What the research found, in English, where it checked each fact, and what the deep research must settle.

writes.text: The main branch
is at

blocks.name: merged
blocks.what: That the work's branch is merged into main, and the head of main it made.

blocks.name: needs_testing
blocks.what: yes when the change is of a kind that goes wrong silently, which only tests written to break it find (a compiler, a checker, a runtime, a data format, concurrency, security, parsing), or as the project's standard for adversarial testing says where it gives one; no otherwise.

blocks.name: place
blocks.what: Where the work is done: its branch, its worktree, and the commit of main it started from.

blocks.name: plan_agent
blocks.what: The plan for the implementation, in English: what changes where, and how each part is verified, with the tests red before the change and green after; each claim it rests on marked verified, with where, or inferred, with how to confirm it.

blocks.name: plan_doubts
blocks.what: What the implementation says to the plan's writer, in English: where and why the plan does not hold.

blocks.name: plan_ok
blocks.what: yes when nothing in the plan must change; no otherwise.

blocks.name: plan_owner
blocks.what: The plan for the owner, in `owner.language`, technical terms in English: what will be done, how and why, no longer than that; where the facts differ from what the item says, that too; each question pointed to where it belongs.

blocks.name: plan_review
blocks.what: What the review of the plan says to its writer, in English: each point, where, what must change and why, what it rests on.

blocks.name: questions
blocks.what: The questions the cells ask the owner, each under its name.

blocks.name: reply_check
blocks.what: The implementation's answer to `check`: fixed, with its commit, or why the check is not this change's.

blocks.name: reply_plan_doubts
blocks.what: The plan's writer's answer to each point of `plan_doubts`: changed, or why not.

blocks.name: reply_plan_review
blocks.what: The plan's writer's answer to each point of `plan_review`: changed, or why not.

blocks.name: reply_review
blocks.what: The implementation's answer to each point of `review`: fixed, with its commit, or why not.

blocks.name: reply_testing
blocks.what: The implementation's answer to each point of `testing`: fixed, with its commit, or why not.

blocks.name: reply_tree_review
blocks.what: The plan's writer's answer to each point of `tree_review`: changed, or why not.

blocks.name: review
blocks.what: What the review says to the implementation, in English: each point, where, what must change and why, what it rests on.

blocks.name: review_ok
blocks.what: yes when nothing in the change must change; no otherwise.

writes.text: The owner started the work.

blocks.name: testing
blocks.what: What the testing says to the implementation, in English: each test that stays red, with what goes wrong by its reference; each place suspected but not tested, such as what shows only on one machine or under concurrency, with why not.

blocks.name: testing_ok
blocks.what: yes when none of the testing's tests is red on the commit `code` names and no suspicion stands; no otherwise.

blocks.name: tests
blocks.what: Each test the testing wrote, with what it checks, its reference, its kind, its results after and before, how long it runs alone and what it catches that no other test does; and the commit that holds them.

blocks.name: tree
blocks.what: The design tree as the work's branch has it: the commit and its tree; between two versions, the files of `design/` that changed.

blocks.name: tree_edits
blocks.what: Each entry the plan adds, changes or deletes in the design tree, as it will read.

blocks.name: tree_ok
blocks.what: yes when nothing in the plan must change for the design tree; no otherwise.

blocks.name: tree_review
blocks.what: What the review against the design tree says to the plan's writer, in English: each point, where, what must change and why, what it rests on.
